source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Write down the date and time of the fire-safety check.
3. Clearly identify the building where the check took place, including address and any specific identifier (like a name or registration number).
4. Note the name and contact information of the person(s) conducting the inspection, as well as their qualifications or affiliation (e.g., fire marshal, safety inspector).
5. Document the exact nature of the failed check, detailing the specific fire-safety measures that were not up to code or malfunctioning. Be specific and descriptive. For example, a fire alarm system that was not functioning properly would be documented as "Fire Alarm System failed to operate properly; no alarm sounded upon activation", noting whether it was due to system failure, lost power, battery issues, or any other pertinent detail.
6. Mention if any parts of the building or systems were not accessible for inspection and explain why.
7. Provide details on any observed hazards or issues that may have contributed
